subject: PhysNet site preflight: cluster footprint, node tiers, and PV resilience
messages:
From: Danielle Wu <dwu@asterhealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@asterhealth.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Intro: PhysNet preflight and site constraints

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for taking this on. We're getting ready to sign an SOW for our first private deployment of Redwood in our primary datacenter (PhysNet DC-1). Before procurement and rack scheduling, the ops team asked for a compact preflight that covers:

- expected cluster footprint (control plane + workers),
- recommended node tiers (gpu vs cpu, sizing guidance),
- persistent volume types and an eviction/resilience matrix,
- networking rules (physical segmentation, egress gating), and
- any hard blockers for air-gapped vs VPC-like private networking.

We have two racks reserved (16U each) and constrained power: 60A per rack. We also have a single top-of-rack switch with limited L3 features today. Can you advise on minimal viable topology and call-outs for our SOW?

Danielle
Site Reliability Lead, AsterHealth

Attachment: site-dc1-power-layout.pdf (figure stub)

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Wu <dwu@asterhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro: PhysNet preflight and site constraints

Danielle — thanks, this is exactly the right time to align. High-level answers below and a quick checklist attached. Will follow up with node-tier numbers once I confirm rack-level thermal/power details.

Short answers:
- Minimal footprint: 3 control-plane VMs (HA) spread across racks + 6 worker nodes for initial capacity (mix of 2 GPU and 4 CPU) for the first phase.
- Node tiers: we recommend a dedicated GPU tier for model-serving (A100/RTX-class) and a CPU tier for orchestration, logging, and light inference.
- PV strategy: fast local NVMe for KV cache and checkpoints (local PV with replication), networked block storage for durable models (iSCSI/FC with HA controller).
- Networking: require L3 routing between racks, multicast not needed; BGP-less fabric OK but you need VLAN and ACLs to separate mgmt/control plane, model-serving, and tenant traffic.
- Air-gap notes: if you go air-gapped, plan for a local package repository and an image registry; also need time sync and attestation flow for binary approvals.

I've attached a two-page preflight checklist (physnet_preflight_checklist_v1.pdf) that lists the specific measurements we need from your site team (switch model, MTU limits, power per PDU, rack U allocation). Can you get those by Monday?

Next steps:
1) Kimberly will propose node-sizing and PV classes.
2) I will map those to the SOW rack BOM and call out optional burst/baremetal lanes.
3) Marcus will own the rollout plan and cutover blackout windows.

Thanks — Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: physnet_preflight_checklist_v1.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Danielle Wu <dwu@asterhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro: PhysNet preflight and site constraints

Adding concrete node tier proposals based on site constraints and the typical workload profile you described (latency-sensitive model serving + background batch transforms):

Proposal (initial phase):
- control-plane: 3x c8.large VMs (8vCPU / 32GB) for kube-apiserver/etcd proxies — we prefer control-plane split across racks for rack-failure tolerance.
- gpu-tier: 2x p4d-equivalent nodes (8xA100 or 4xH100 per node depending on vendor) with 1TB NVMe local for KV/cache.
- cpu-tier: 4x m8.large nodes (32vCPU / 256GB) for model workers, batch jobs, and sidecars.

Storage classes & resilience:
- local-fast (NVMe): ephemeral + scheduled replication using a synchronous dual-writer service for checkpoints. Recommended for cache and low-latency checkpoints only; DO NOT use for master state.
- durable-block (iSCSI/FC): for model artifacts and long-lived storage. Configure replication across a storage-controller pair in separate racks.
- object-backup (S3-compatible on-prem): for large model tarballs and offsite backup replication.

Eviction & QoS: configure guaranteed QoS for model-serving pods (reserve CPU/memory) and best-effort for batch. Set eviction thresholds: node fs.available < 10% or disk pressure triggers migration. Add a PV-resilience matrix (attached pv-resilience-matrix.csv) that maps data class to backup cadence and RTO goals.

Open questions for Aster ops:
- Are you able to provide separate L3 VLANs for mgmt/control vs tenant egress?
- Do you have an internal iSCSI controller with replication across racks or should we plan for an external SAN?

I'll drop an XLS with per-node cost and a rack-BOM (node_tier_proposal.xlsx) shortly.

—Kimberly
Head of Field Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachments: node_tier_proposal.xlsx; pv-resilience-matrix.csv

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

1) Danielle / Aster ops: please send the site checklist answers and the switch model + firmware by EOD Wednesday. Those will determine whether we can rely on per-packet ACLs or need an overlay for segmentation.
2) Priyom: once you get rack thermal/power confirmation, update the BOM and indicate if we must shift to lower-power GPU options.
3) Kimberly: finalize the node_tier_proposal.xlsx and include the uplift for NVMe-backed scratch (10% spare per node).

Rollout timeline (tentative):

- Week 1: network cabling, rack power test
- Week 2: control-plane install + bootstrap (canary tenant)
- Week 3: GPU tier deploy + model validation

I'll create the rollout calendar in the shared Drive and send a DocuSign SOW draft once the BOM is locked.

Marcus Lin
Senior Program Manager, Field Deployments, Redwood Inference
